corrections.reason: The same idea from Grade 3 is missing. Seeing that 1/2 and 5/10 name the same amount is the idea that different fractions can name the same amount, which is what g3-equivalent-fair-shares teaches (one fifth and two tenths). No other listed prerequisite depends on g3-equivalent-fair-shares, so it is a direct prerequisite.

Comparing and ordering decimals such as 24.7 and 3.2 requires comparing the whole-number parts, which is the Grade 3 comparing skill. Neither g3-place-value nor g4-represent-fractions depends on g3-compare-order-1000, so it is direct.

The splitting strategy produces partial products, such as 60 and 12, that the kid must add to finish. That needs mental addition of numbers up to 1000 (g3-mental-math-1000). No other listed prerequisite depends on it, so it is direct.

output.notes: Reviewed all 17 proposed Grade 4 skills. All prerequisites are from Grade 3 or earlier, or from earlier Grade 4 skills, and none point to the skill itself. The titles and descriptions match their expectations and read aloud well. Three skills had a missing direct prerequisite and are corrected above. I left the other prerequisite lists unchanged. Where a needed Grade 3 idea is already reached through a listed prerequisite (for example g3-place-value, g3-fair-share-20, g3-fraction-repeated-addition, and g3-add-sub-algorithms), adding it directly would break the directness rule, so I did not add it. g4-mult-div-by-10s keeps g4-decimal-tenths, because the skill says "divide it by 10" for any number, which can give tenths.
